title: Fonts with next/font
summary: `next/font` lets you use Google or local fonts that are **automatically self-hosted**, optimized, and applied with **zero layout shift** and **no requests to Google** — improving performance and privacy with almost no setup.

subtopics.title: next/font/google
subtopics.explanation: Import any Google Font as a function. At build time Next downloads the font files and serves them from YOUR domain, so no request is ever made to Google at runtime. You configure subsets, weights, and display directly in the import call.
subtopics.example:
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google';
const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] });

subtopics.title: next/font/local
subtopics.explanation: Use font files you ship yourself (e.g. a licensed brand font in /public or /app). You point `src` at the file(s), and Next handles loading, optimization, and the same zero-layout-shift behavior as Google fonts.
subtopics.example:
import localFont from 'next/font/local';
const brand = localFont({ src: './Brand.woff2' });

subtopics.title: Automatic self-hosting
subtopics.explanation: next/font fetches font files at build time and bundles them into your app's static assets. The browser only ever talks to your origin/CDN, which removes a third-party network hop and the privacy concerns of Google's font CDN.
subtopics.example: // No <link> to fonts.googleapis.com is ever emitted.

subtopics.title: Zero layout shift (size-adjust)
subtopics.explanation: Custom fonts often arrive after the page paints, causing text to jump (CLS) as the fallback is swapped. next/font precomputes a matched fallback using the CSS `size-adjust` / `ascent-override` descriptors so the fallback occupies the same space, eliminating the shift.
subtopics.example: /* Generated @font-face includes size-adjust to match the fallback metrics */

subtopics.title: Subsetting
subtopics.explanation: A font's full file contains glyphs for many scripts. Specifying `subsets` (e.g. ['latin']) ships only the glyphs you need, dramatically shrinking the downloaded font and speeding first paint.

subtopics.title: Variable fonts
subtopics.explanation: Variable fonts pack many weights/styles into one file via axes, so you don't list discrete `weight` values. They're the recommended default with next/font because one file covers the whole weight range efficiently.
subtopics.example: Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] }); // variable: no weight array needed

subtopics.title: Applying via className
subtopics.explanation: The font object returns a `className` you spread onto an element (commonly <body> or <html> in the root layout). Everything inside inherits the font with no global CSS edits.

subtopics.title: Applying via CSS variable
subtopics.explanation: Set `variable: '--font-inter'` and use the object's `.variable` class to expose the font as a CSS custom property, which you then reference in CSS (or a Tailwind config). This is ideal when you mix multiple fonts.

foundations.overview: next/font is Next.js's built-in font system. You import a Google or local font as a function, configure it once, and apply its className (or a CSS variable) in your layout. Behind the scenes Next self-hosts the files, subsets them, and injects fallback metrics so text never shifts.
foundations.formalDefinition: next/font is a build-time font optimization API (next/font/google and next/font/local) that downloads, subsets, and self-hosts font files, generates @font-face rules with metric-matched fallbacks, and returns a className/style + CSS variable for applying the font.
foundations.whyItMatters: Fonts are a top cause of layout shift (CLS) and a hidden third-party request. next/font removes both problems automatically, so you get better Core Web Vitals and user privacy without writing font-loading code yourself.
foundations.mentalModel: Think of the font import as a 'compiled asset': you describe the font you want (family, subset, display), and at build time Next turns that description into self-hosted files plus the exact @font-face CSS needed to render it shift-free.
foundations.browserPerspective: The browser downloads the font from your own origin (no fonts.googleapis.com hop), paints text immediately using a size-adjusted fallback, then swaps to the real font with no visible jump because the fallback already occupied the right space.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Almost every Next.js app sets a primary font in the root layout via next/font/google, and brand-heavy sites add a licensed font through next/font/local. Multi-font designs expose each as a CSS variable.
foundations.businessImpact: Lower CLS and faster text paint improve Core Web Vitals, which affect SEO ranking and conversion. Removing Google's font CDN also helps GDPR/privacy compliance by avoiding sending user IPs to a third party.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Developers stop hand-writing @font-face rules, preconnect hints, and font-display hacks. The font is declared once and inherited, reducing styling bugs and boilerplate.
foundations.performanceImpact: Self-hosting cuts a DNS/connection to a third party; subsetting shrinks the font payload; size-adjust fallbacks eliminate CLS; and fonts are preloaded only on routes that use them.
commonUseCases: Setting a single app-wide font in the root layout
Shipping a licensed/brand font via next/font/local
Exposing multiple fonts as CSS variables for headings vs body
Reducing CLS and Core Web Vitals failures caused by web fonts

commonMisconceptions.myth: next/font fetches fonts from Google at runtime.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Fonts are downloaded at BUILD time and self-hosted on your domain; the browser never contacts Google's CDN.

commonMisconceptions.myth: You must manually add font-display and preconnect to avoid layout shift.
commonMisconceptions.reality: next/font generates a metric-matched fallback (size-adjust) and handles preloading automatically, so you don't write that boilerplate.

config.intro: Trace what next/font does at build time and what the browser does at runtime.

steps.name: Declare
steps.detail: You import the font as a function and pass options (subsets, display, weight/variable). This is a build-time declaration, not a runtime fetch.

steps.name: Download & subset
steps.detail: At build, Next downloads the font files from Google (or reads your local files) and subsets them to only the glyphs you requested.

steps.name: Self-host
steps.detail: The optimized files are emitted as your app's static assets, so they're served from your origin/CDN — never from a third party at runtime.

steps.name: Generate @font-face
steps.detail: Next writes @font-face rules including size-adjust/ascent-override so a system fallback matches the real font's metrics.

steps.name: Apply
steps.detail: You add the returned className (or CSS variable) to an element; everything inside inherits the font.

steps.name: Render
steps.detail: The browser paints text with the matched fallback instantly, then swaps to the real font with zero layout shift.

debuggingLab.title: Font causes a layout shift on load
debuggingLab.symptom: Text reflows/jumps a moment after the page appears, hurting CLS — the team loads the font with a manual <link> and font-display: swap.
debuggingLab.errorAnalysis: A manual <link> to Google Fonts makes a runtime third-party request AND uses a generic fallback whose metrics don't match Inter. When Inter finally loads, line-height/width change and the layout shifts (CLS). It also leaks user IPs to Google.
commonMistakes: Loading fonts via a hand-written <link> to fonts.googleapis.com.
Relying on font-display: swap alone, which still shifts because the fallback metrics differ.
debuggingLab.fixChallenge: Replace the manual link with next/font/google so the font is self-hosted with a size-adjusted fallback.

theory.question: What does next/font do and why use it instead of a Google Fonts <link>?
theory.directAnswer: next/font downloads and self-hosts font files at build time, subsets them, and generates @font-face rules with a metric-matched fallback (size-adjust) so there's zero layout shift. Compared to a manual Google Fonts <link>, it removes the third-party runtime request (better speed and privacy) and prevents CLS automatically.

detailedExplanation.whatItIs: A built-in font optimization API with next/font/google and next/font/local.
detailedExplanation.whyItExists: Web fonts are a common source of layout shift and a hidden third-party request; next/font solves both with no boilerplate.
detailedExplanation.howItWorks: At build time it fetches/optimizes the files, emits them as static assets served from your origin, and injects @font-face with size-adjust so the fallback matches the real font's metrics.

theory.whyImportant: Fonts directly affect Core Web Vitals (CLS, paint timing) and privacy compliance, both of which come up in real apps and interviews.
theory.realWorldExample: Setting Inter app-wide in app/layout.tsx via inter.className gives self-hosted, shift-free text with one import.

nestedTopics.title: Self-hosting
nestedTopics.explanation: Files are served from your domain, removing the Google CDN hop at runtime.

nestedTopics.title: Size-adjust
nestedTopics.explanation: Generated @font-face descriptors make the fallback occupy the same space, eliminating CLS.

followUps.question: Where do you usually apply the font?
followUps.answer: On <html> or <body> in the root layout via the returned className, so all routes inherit it.

theory.question: How does next/font achieve zero layout shift, and what is subsetting?
theory.directAnswer: Zero layout shift comes from a metric-matched fallback: next/font computes size-adjust/ascent-override descriptors so the system fallback takes the same space as the real font, so swapping in the real font doesn't move anything. Subsetting means shipping only the glyphs you need (e.g. the 'latin' subset) instead of the full multi-script file, which shrinks the download and speeds first paint.

detailedExplanation.whatItIs: Two optimizations: metric-matched fallbacks for CLS, and glyph subsetting for payload size.
detailedExplanation.whyItExists: Mismatched fallbacks cause text to reflow, and full font files are large; both hurt performance.
detailedExplanation.howItWorks: Next reads the font's metrics to generate the adjusted fallback and slices the font to the requested `subsets`.

theory.whyImportant: Understanding these explains why next/font beats a manual font load and shows you grasp Core Web Vitals.
theory.realWorldExample: Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] }) ships only Latin glyphs and renders with no jump even on slow networks.

nestedTopics.title: Variable fonts
nestedTopics.explanation: One file covers the full weight range, so you usually omit the weight array.

followUps.question: Do you still need font-display: swap?
followUps.answer: You can set it, but the metric-matched fallback is what actually prevents the shift; display just controls the swap behavior.

scenario.question: A site fails Core Web Vitals due to font-driven CLS and also flags a privacy review for contacting Google's font CDN. How do you fix both?
scenario.directAnswer: Replace the manual Google Fonts <link> with next/font/google. That self-hosts the files (so the browser never contacts Google, clearing the privacy flag) and generates a size-adjusted fallback (so the CLS from font swap disappears). For brand fonts, use next/font/local with the licensed files.

detailedExplanation.whatItIs: A combined performance + privacy fix via next/font.
detailedExplanation.whyItExists: Manual font links cause both issues at once.
detailedExplanation.howItWorks: Build-time self-hosting + metric-matched fallback addresses the network hop and the layout shift together.

scenario.whyImportant: It's a common real-world cleanup that improves SEO/UX and compliance simultaneously.

nestedTopics.title: next/font/local
nestedTopics.explanation: Use for licensed/brand fonts you ship yourself, with the same optimizations.

followUps.question: How do you confirm Google is no longer contacted?
followUps.answer: Check the network tab/HTML — there should be no request to fonts.googleapis.com or fonts.gstatic.com.

coding.question: Set up Inter as the app-wide font and a local brand font as a CSS variable in the App Router.
coding.thoughtProcess: I'll import Inter from next/font/google and apply its className to <html> for app-wide use. For the brand font I'll use next/font/local with a variable, and apply both classes so I can reference the brand font via var(--font-brand) in CSS.
coding.lineByLine: Inter() returns a className applied to <html> so all text uses Inter by default. localFont() with `variable` exposes the brand font as --font-brand; applying brand.variable makes that variable available, and CSS uses it for headings only.

alternativeApproaches.title: Variable for the primary font too
alternativeApproaches.explanation: Expose the main font as a CSS variable instead of className for full control in CSS/Tailwind.

followUps.question: Why apply the font in the layout rather than each page?
followUps.answer: The root layout wraps every route, so applying once makes the whole app inherit the font with no duplication.

productionDeepDive.architecture: Declare fonts in the root layout (or a shared module) so they're applied once and inherited. Use className for a single global font and CSS variables when combining multiple fonts (e.g. heading vs body), wiring the variables into your CSS or Tailwind theme.
productionDeepDive.performance: next/font self-hosts and preloads fonts only on routes that use them, subsets glyphs to shrink payloads, and uses size-adjust fallbacks to eliminate CLS. Prefer variable fonts to avoid shipping many weight files.
productionDeepDive.security: Self-hosting removes a third-party origin, reducing supply-chain and tracking surface. There are no runtime requests carrying user IPs to a font CDN.
productionDeepDive.scaling: Fonts become regular static assets served from your CDN, so they scale like any other static file; per-route preloading keeps unused fonts off pages that don't need them.
productionDeepDive.maintainability: Centralizing font config in one module keeps families/weights consistent and makes swapping a font a one-line change instead of editing scattered @font-face rules.
productionDeepDive.observability: Track CLS and font load timing via Core Web Vitals tooling (e.g. Vercel Speed Insights, Lighthouse) to confirm no shift and verify there are no third-party font requests in the network panel.

caseStudies.problem: Loading Google Fonts via <link> sent user IPs to Google and caused GDPR concerns plus font-swap CLS.
caseStudies.solution: Migrated to next/font/google, which self-hosts files at build time and matches fallback metrics.
caseStudies.tradeoffs: Fonts are pinned at build time (a font update requires a rebuild) in exchange for privacy and zero CLS.
caseStudies.lessons: Self-hosting via next/font fixes performance and privacy in one step with minimal code.

keyTakeaways: next/font downloads and self-hosts fonts at BUILD time — the browser never contacts Google's CDN, improving speed and privacy.
It generates a metric-matched (size-adjust) fallback so swapping in the real font causes zero layout shift (CLS).
Use next/font/google for Google fonts and next/font/local for fonts you ship yourself.
Apply a single font with the returned className, or expose multiple fonts as CSS variables (the .variable class).
Set `subsets` (e.g. ['latin']) and prefer variable fonts to keep font payloads small.
